result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make Studio the focal card with several matching cues: an accent border, a shadow, extra padding, a 'Most popular' label, a larger price and the only filled button. Both keep prices dominant and give each card one CTA, with Studio's button the loudest. A has the clearer type hierarchy, because its tier names are larger and bolder than the feature lists. B's equal-height cards with bottom-aligned buttons are easier to compare, but its muted 1rem tier names are barely louder than the features. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B makes Studio stand out more clearly than A. Studio sits higher and is taller, with a filled pill badge on the top edge, a bigger price, and the only filled button. B's tier names are 20px bold, so they rank above the feature list. A keeps all three cards the same height with their buttons in line, which makes them easier to compare. However, A styles its tier names muted while the feature items use the full text color, so the features are not quieter than the names. B's centered alignment leaves Solo shorter than Agency, so its buttons sit at different heights, which weakens it a little on consistent structure.
